summary: Security review of provider/CLI isolation, prompt-injection defenses, secrets handling, docs and live tests. Artifacts match submission hashes. npm test 285/285 pass, live isolation test passes (tools == [StructuredOutput], no MCP/skills/slash commands, no permission denials), env and delimiter probes behave as designed. Remaining items are minor/info. F8 is verified fixed by my own re-run. Release-metric status (M1c) is a quality matter and not human-accepted; I make no acceptance claim.

criteria.description: CLI provider isolation: no shell, no tools, no settings/MCP/slash commands, scrubbed env without the API key, fresh cwd, stdout cap, timeout and process-group kill
Prompt-injection defenses: fixed system prompt, untrusted data in one JSON line between random delimiters with < > U+2028/9 escaped, schema-validated output, verifier downstream
Secrets handling: API key never forwarded to the CLI child, not logged, not committed; error messages are fixed strings; config guidance in README and operations doc is accurate
Cost and abuse limits enforced: per-call USD budget, concurrency semaphore, deadline, retry only on malformed output, eval cap guard working
Live tests are opt-in (GW_LIVE=1), pass an empty-API-key env, and pass when run
Data egress is disclosed to users and operators

findings.title: GW_CLI_ENV_PASS and GW_CLI_MODEL are operator-trusted and unvalidated
findings.detail: Probe: GW_CLI_ENV_PASS=GW_SEED_PASSWORD is forwarded to the child; ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is blocked by name only, other credential names (e.g. ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN) can be passed. buildArgv accepts a model string starting with '--' (e.g. '--dangerously-skip-permissions') as a value of --model; it is a separate argv element so it is consumed as the option value, not a flag, and there is no shell. Both inputs are operator env only, not user input, so impact is low.
findings.recommendation: Optionally reject GW_CLI_ENV_PASS names matching /KEY|TOKEN|SECRET|PASSWORD/ and validate GW_CLI_MODEL against /^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$/ in src/config.js.

findings.title: README usage figures stale (F11) and CLI inherits HOME/CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR
findings.detail: README says eval/usage.log has 15 entries / USD 1.454; the log differs, and operations.md cites 12 tune runs, while checkBudget on the real log reports 12 runs and USD 1.85 logged. Separately the child receives HOME and CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, so it uses the host user's CLI credentials by design; --setting-sources '' limits config loading but the egress to Anthropic is as documented.
findings.recommendation: Refresh the README figures from usage.log; state that CLI auth comes from the host user's login.

findings.title: Prompt-injection resistance is statistical, and docs-level open items remain
findings.detail: Defenses rely on model compliance plus schema validation and verifier flagging; M4 covers 10 injection cases only. Unconfirmed: novel payloads. Also noted by the author: no health/provider metrics, no .env.example, SIGTERM to the npm wrapper does not stop the server. No human acceptance of thresholds or the tune-run overrun is recorded; that decision remains with the user.
findings.recommendation: Keep the human-review step before publish; expand injection corpus in future work.

resolvedFindings.resolution: checkBudget on the real usage.log now returns fullTuneRuns 12 and ok:false (cap of 8 refuses further runs); budget tests pass 5/5; the overrun is disclosed in docs.
